author: agent
text:
Re-read at 0.57.2. Every comment in this visitor checked against the body; all still describe it, and the rot flag fired because the emission gained a field, not because anything it says stopped being true. The annotated-receiver and forward-ref reasoning is unchanged, and dst_override still means "the parser resolved the receiver to a module, so ship the qualified name".

WHAT CHANGED, and the distinction is load-bearing. RawEdge now carries `bare` alongside `via_attr`, and they are NOT the same question:

  via_attr = dst_override is None and isinstance(n.func, ast.Attribute)
  bare     = not isinstance(n.func, ast.Attribute)

via_attr answers "an attribute call the parser could NOT resolve to a module" - it is deliberately cleared when dst_override names the target, because the attribute-call rule must not fire on a reference the parser already qualified. That makes it unable to answer "was a receiver written at all", which is what the builtin rule needs.

I reused via_attr for that and it was wrong: every resolved-receiver call to a method was refused, and rich and sqlalchemy fell below their corpus recall floors in the first network run. The floors caught it; no fixture did. Keep the two fields separate - merging them will look like a simplification and will silently delete edges.

author: cli
text: Re-read at the literal-receiver change. The bare/via_attr distinction recorded below is unchanged and still load-bearing. A THIRD field joins them - literal_recv, set by _py_literal_recv - for the reason the confirm below gives about the first two: they answer different questions and merging them deletes edges. The reasoning and measurements live on memway.edges.EdgeBuilder._unreachable_target.
